behindBrand.subtitle: How Atlantic Ave came to be and what stands behind it
behindBrand.closingText: Every piece is the result of this process. In limited numbers.
s1Body: The idea for my own brand was born while I was living in America. It wasn't a clear plan or a specific goal. More like a feeling that would surface now and then, and fade away again.

But after I came back to the Czech Republic, the idea wouldn't let go of me. It came back every day. I kept turning it over in my head, until one day I stumbled on a video of two guys spray-painting T-shirts. And I told myself: why not give it a try?

At that moment I had no plan for it to ever become a real brand. I wasn't thinking about production, factories, printing, packaging or an e-shop. It was just about taking the first step and trying something out.
s2Body: When I realized that spray-painting wasn't the right path, I started looking more into classic printing and real garment production. I ordered the first pieces. Tried printing the first designs. I tested. I learned.
And somewhere along the way it hit me that I wasn't really testing anymore. That something with its own direction was slowly taking shape.

All of it came together without a big budget. Without room for pointless mistakes. I had to weigh every decision far more than I might have wanted to. And that is exactly what taught me to care about every detail.
s3Body: I try to put everything into each piece. That doesn't mean everything is always perfect — but it means I won't release anything into the world just because 'it would probably do'.
Often fifty designs get made and only two of them are used. I take the rest as a necessary part of the journey, not as a mistake. Without them, those two final ones would never have existed.
This approach shows in everything I create — whether it's the cut itself, the material, the print or the smallest details.
s4Body: I was there for all of it. From finding factories to printing, cuts and materials, all the way to labels, packaging, stickers and the e-shop itself.

Not because I didn't trust others, but because I wanted to understand the whole process. To find out how things are made. What really affects quality. What makes the difference between an average and a great piece.
It wasn't just about looking good. I wanted it to wear well. To last. To still make sense a year from now, not just today.
s5Body: Atlantic Ave runs on the principle of smaller, limited collections.
It's not about churning out as many garments as possible. I want to create things I can stand behind one hundred percent.
The first official drop sold out. I don't take that as proof that I 'know it all' now. I take it more as huge confirmation that this approach makes sense.
s6Body: Atlantic Ave isn't a finished thing. It's a process that evolves with every next step.
I'm learning. I'm getting better. And I always try to do things a little better than last time.
